scope: Six- and eleven-board mechanical stress collections from real VAIO sources. Includes alternative revisions; not an electrically qualified complete VAIO product. No custom harness was created.
features: Up to 12 deterministic board orders and obstacle-edge placement candidates
Layout comparisons run in a Web Worker; native intersection checks stay in Preview
Optional conservative 3D cable corridors, bend radii, routed length and previously planned cable reservations
Assumed screwdriver access checks for mounting holes
Planar artwork excluded before solid conversion; per-board temporary solids released; failed boards do not exhaust later board budgets

broaderWindowsPackages.note: Four existing CLI-probe shim failures and one CRLF-sensitive stencil fixture failure; the same five occur in prior baseline-compared logs. Protocol, client-core and UI packages pass.

tests.previousCiFailureFixed: Updated the measured-aperture fixture to provide dimension evidence; unknown values are still tested as review items.

limitations: Bounded search does not prove a global optimum.

Cable planning uses conservative boxes and a limited set of orthogonal detours; connector exits, flat-ribbon orientation, exact holder/lug geometry and physical cable specifications need review. Cables are reserved sequentially, not globally optimized.
No verified inter-board cable map was supplied for this collection; real layout benchmarks do not claim verified cable reach.
Combined peripheral A2 needs KiCad 10.99 or later; its native body remains unavailable on the installed KiCad 10.0.
Missing component models, actual screw/tool dimensions, retention and electrical compatibility remain review items.
Cooling, mass distribution, material strength, screw pullout and physical assembly are not simulated or certified.
Print-area planning limits the rectangular case body. Exported hardware and slicer placement must still be checked.
